Today's verdict NEUTRAL-CAUTIOUS
When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Nasdaq 100 **+6.2%** over five days vs VIX backwardation and skew both active, risk-off bias with **3** signals aligned
Price shows strength while options traders pay up for protection. Trust the options market for risk sizing, because it prices the next move and the rally shows only the last one. Trust price for direction until backwardation resolves.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **55**, ACCUMULATE partial signal vs Regime state **61**, TRANSITION with a risk-off bias
One gauge invites buying weakness while the other says conditions are deteriorating. Trust the regime read for pacing: the contrarian signal is only partial at **55**, so stage any entries in small pieces.

Nasdaq is ripping while volatility signals and the regime read lean defensive
Bull

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The market is split between a loud price rally and a cautious options market. The Nasdaq 100 is up +6.2% in five days, yet the Crash Index reads 4/10 and the regime score is 61, which is a transition with 3 risk-off signals aligned. You should trust the caution while the rally lacks confirmation.

The VIX Spike Detector sits at tier 2 of 4 with a 60% probability reading. Skew and backwardation are both active, so traders are paying for near-term protection even as index prices climb. Add the macro regime, which reads CONTRACTION at only 40% confidence, and you get a backdrop that is leaning weak but is far from settled.

For positioning, keep gross exposure moderate and let the contrarian reading of 55 guide small, staged entries rather than one large buy. Hedges are cheap relative to what the options market is signaling, so own some. The divergence picture adds weight: 48.8% of tracked pairs are pulling apart from their usual relationships, which means correlations you rely on may not hold.

The main risk is that backwardation deepens and the Crash Index climbs past 4/10 while Nasdaq leadership stalls. The reading that flips the stance to constructive is backwardation fading while the +6.2% gain holds and the regime score improves from 61.

AI read · macro regime

The regime reads CONTRACTION, but confidence is only 40%. That is a weak call, and it fits the transition label on the regime score of 61.

A contraction backdrop favors quality, shorter duration in your risk, and cash held ready. The low confidence and the strength in the Nasdaq 100 argue against going fully defensive.

Position for a regime that could break either way: trim the most extended winners, keep core holdings, and keep dry powder for the contrarian signal if it climbs above 55. A rise in regime confidence above 40% with the same CONTRACTION label would be your cue to cut harder.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that normally move together are starting to move apart. Correlation drift is the measure of that shift: how tightly the pair moved before versus how it moves now.

The composite zone is ELEVATED, with 48.8% of 43 tracked pairs diverging, and the mother jaws score hits 100. The bearish count is 13 against 8 bullish, a net bias of 5 toward the bearish side.

The six deepest pairs each score 80. Copper against gold shifted from +0.85 to -0.09, so the growth signal and the safe-haven signal no longer agree.

Gold against Treasuries went from -0.51 to +0.66, meaning both are now moving together, which is unusual and points to a hunt for safety. ARKK against SPY went from +0.04 to +0.63, so speculative growth is now tied to the broad index.

Energy against tech moved from -0.96 to -0.20, the old seesaw weakening. Many of the usual hedging relationships are loosening, so diversification is less dependable than it looks.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Leadership today is clear. The US leads with the Nasdaq 100 at +6.2% over five days, while the Dow trails at +1.5%.

That gap shows growth and tech carrying the gains. Europe is up as well: the STOXX 50 gained +2.0% and the FTSE only +0.1%.

In Asia, the KOSPI rose +2.0% and the Shanghai Composite slipped -0.2%, so strength is concentrated in tech-heavy markets. Crypto goes the other way, with Bitcoin down -6.1% and Ethereum down -10.1% over the same five days.

Crypto is a risk-appetite barometer that trades around the clock, and its weakness while the Nasdaq surges is a warning that speculative appetite is thinner than the equity move implies. For the US session, expect tech to keep leading but watch for fading follow-through if crypto keeps sliding.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 4/10 · WARNING — 3+ signals, active surveillance
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 4/10 and the VIX Spike Detector at tier 2 of 4 agree more than they differ. Both sit in the middle, which fits a market that has rallied but is not at ease.

The Crash Index measures damage already visible in price and breadth. The Spike Detector measures what options traders expect next.

With skew active, backwardation active, and a 60% spike probability, the options market is pricing more turbulence than the calm surface of the Nasdaq 100 suggests. That gap is a coherent state: price is rising while buyers of protection get more aggressive.

The adaptive trigger is off, so the signal has not reached its most urgent setting. Treat this as a watch state.

A move to tier 3, or a Crash Index above 4/10, would shift you from hedging at the edges to cutting exposure.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 4/10 — a few early signals are stirring; watch whether more line up.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
